facts.text: The grey teal is a mottled brown dabbling duck with white and green flashes on its wings, and adults have a striking crimson iris.
facts.quote: It is identified by the presence of a crimson coloured iris in its eyes, which is relatively more prominent in adult males. It is a mottled brown duck with white and green flashes on its wings.

facts.text: The grey teal is a vocal duck, especially at night, with the male giving a soft preep and the female a loud quack.
facts.quote: It is a vocal duck, especially at night. The male gives a soft preep, and the female has a loud quack.

facts.text: In Australia, grey teal eat mostly plant material, especially seeds, which make up 87–97% of their diet.
facts.quote: Thus, in Australia grey teal feed mostly on plant material and especially seeds. It constitutes 87–97% of their diet.

facts.text: Grey teal are nomadic in Australia, rapidly colonising suitable habitat after rain, and in 1957 large numbers fled to New Zealand to escape a drought.
facts.quote: It is nomadic in Australia, rapidly colonising suitable habitat following rain. In 1957, large numbers fled Australia, moving to New Zealand to escape a drought.

facts.text: Grey teal pairs are long-term and monogamous, keeping the same mate through multiple seasons and staying together all year.
facts.quote: This is because grey teal pair-bonds are long term and monogamous, which means they keep the same mate through multiple seasons. Couples stay together all year

facts.text: In Australia, grey teal have no fixed breeding season; breeding is linked to rainfall and food abundance.
facts.quote: In Australia there is no reproductive season as breeding is linked to rainfall and food abundance.

facts.text: While the female incubates the eggs for 25–31 days, the male stands guard and protects her and the eggs.
facts.quote: During the incubation period, the male will stand guard and protect the female and eggs while she incubates them for 25–31 days.

facts.text: Grey teal fly remarkable distances, with recorded flights of up to 1,200 km across the arid Australian inland in search of water.
facts.quote: these flights occurred over distances up to 1,200 km (750 mi) across the arid inland.

facts.text: In Australia the grey teal is a game bird hunted by duck shooters, but in New Zealand it is protected due to low population numbers.
facts.quote: However, in Australia, they are considered a game bird due to large population numbers. Therefore hunters and duck shooters are a significant predator of these birds; whereas in New Zealand the grey teal is a protected species.
